clue.text: Cop later injured — medicine chest needed?

indicators.note: injured suggests the words cop later are damaged and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman gets hurt and someone calls for the first-aid box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medicine chest' looks like a first-aid box; read it as medicine for the chest. 'Injured' rearranges COP LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pectoral is a remedy for complaints of the lungs and breast, so it is the medicine a sore chest needs.

clue.text: Mathematician needing some help as calculator

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mathematician who needs a little help from an adding machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Blaise Pascal, the French mathematician, built one of the first mechanical calculators, so the surface fits him.
explanation.definitionFit: Blaise Pascal was a seventeenth-century French thinker famed for probability theory and geometry.

clue.text: Coach and horse in accident, almost

indicators.note: in places the horse inside the shortened word for accident
almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: chance means an accident, as in 'by chance'
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A coach and horses involved in a near crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach and horse' paints a carriage scene, but the coach is the definition and the horse is an Arab inside a shortened accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc is an old open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Oppressive old despot over us

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the despot sits above the word us

parts.note: Nero was a tyrannical Roman emperor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A former tyrant lording it over us is burdensome.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous duty is heavy and burdensome to bear.

clue.text: Fraternity formed in American university within a year

indicators.note: within puts the university inside the letters for a and year

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A college fraternity founded at a US university some time in the past year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fraternity' suggests an American student club; here it means friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendly relations, the brotherly feeling of fellowship.

clue.text: Reflecting sound choice when the last comes first

indicators.note: the final letter of the word choice is carried round to stand at its front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction about picking a sound by putting the last option first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When the last comes first' moves the closing E of CHOICE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoic words imitate or echo a noise, so they reflect sound back like an echo.

clue.text: Way in which Tom may have altered flat cap

indicators.note: altered says the letters of flat cap are changed round

explanation.surface: A man has changed the shape of his cloth cap.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name; a tom is a male cat, which enters a house through a small hinged door.
explanation.definitionFit: A small swinging door in a house door lets a pet come and go, the route by which a male cat gets in.

clue.text: European flower said to produce scent

indicators.note: said to produce says the river's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a flower here is something that flows, a river; the Oder runs between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A Continental bloom is reported to give off a perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick for a river (something that flows), here the Oder.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, so a perfume is one kind.

clue.text: Window box soundly designed

parts.note: a case is a box

indicators.note: soundly signals that the next word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: meant means designed or intended

explanation.surface: A window box that is well put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'well'; it tells you MEANT (designed) is heard, giving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a window hinged at the side so it opens like a door.

clue.text: Poem one's written inside Valentine, perhaps

indicators.note: written inside puts the word one within the word for a poem

parts.note: verse means a poem
one, the 's being 'is'

explanation.surface: A poem written inside a Valentine's card.
explanation.walkthrough: Valentine is not a card but one of Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona, so a native of Verona.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentine in Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen comes from Verona, so he is an example of a citizen of that city.

clue.text: Guidance for players in courses provided by coach

indicators.note: provided by means the coach word supplies its piece and stands at the front

parts.note: a stage, or stagecoach, is an old horse-drawn coach
courses are directions or routes taken

explanation.surface: Advice for sportsmen on which courses to run, given by their coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'coach' suggest sport; the players are actors and the coach is a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes in a script telling actors where to move and what to do guide those performers.

clue.text: Detailed analysis can reveal tiny amount, in any case

indicators.note: in, with 'any case', says one piece is enclosed by the word any as its case

parts.note: taken as written
an atom is a tiny amount, as in 'not an atom of truth'

explanation.surface: A close study can turn up a minute quantity whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In any case' reads as 'whatever happens', but it is a container instruction: the case is the word any.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomy of something is a minute dissection or examination of its parts.

clue.text: Mature spirit I put in fuel container

indicators.note: put in says the letter I is placed inside the word for mature

parts.note: mature means old
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Aged liquor that the speaker pours into a tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal barrel used for storing petroleum products is a container for fuel.

clue.text: It's open to negotiation all right

explanation.surface: Something that can be bargained over is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiation' suggests bargaining; here it means getting across, as a road or river is negotiated.
explanation.definitionFit: A road or ford that can be crossed is traversable, and work that is adequate but not great is satisfactory.

clue.text: Like some rocks, when covered by, sea

indicators.note: covered by says one word is enclosed by the name of the sea

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Some rocks are submerged when the tide comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Basalt is a dark volcanic stone, and basaltic describes rocks made of or resembling it.

clue.text: Peg gets absolutely no money back

indicators.note: back says the combined words are read from right to left

parts.note: no, said absolutely and flatly
a tip is money given as a gratuity

explanation.surface: A man with a peg leg receives not a penny in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses both pieces together as one run, giving the climber's peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike driven into rock by climbers to hold a rope, a kind of peg.

clue.text: Cheats watch clock

explanation.surface: Swindlers keeping an eye on the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'watch' and 'clock' as two nouns: a pair of timepieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfaithful lovers deceive their partners, and a wristwatch with a wall clock make a pair of timepieces.

clue.text: Stress can make one misshape components

indicators.note: components suggests the parts of the word misshape are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Tension can cause someone to deform machine parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Components' treats the letters of MISSHAPE as parts to rearrange; 'can make one' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress placed on a word or point to mark its importance.

clue.text: Parrot initially mimics a cry of another bird

indicators.note: initially picks only the opening letter of the word mimics

parts.note: caw is the call of a crow or rook

explanation.surface: A parrot copies the call of a different bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Spotted raising old-fashioned vessels for this?

definitions.text: Spotted raising old-fashioned vessels for this?

indicators.note: raising, in a down clue, lifts the word for spotted so it reads upwards

parts.note: saw means spotted
sail is an old collective word for ships, as in 'a fleet of forty sail'

explanation.surface: Someone notices old cups being lifted in a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns SAW upward to WAS. The whole clue also hints at raising old cups in a festive drinking toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is a spiced ale drunk at festive toasts, served in a large bowl and raised in salute.

clue.text: Source of cabinet plans to develop North Sea

indicators.note: to develop suggests the words north sea are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Government plans to exploit the North Sea oilfields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' looks political; it is furniture. Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English furniture designer whose pattern books were widely copied.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton published designs for furniture, so cabinet-makers took their patterns from his books.

clue.text: Whence a number left on plane

definitions.text: Whence a number left on plane

parts.words: Whence a number left on plane
parts.note: the place from which many people departed aboard an aircraft, read as a passenger terminal rather than a geometry problem

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle about a number left on a flat surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' and 'number' suggest geometry; the plane is an aircraft and the number is many passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flights depart from an aerodrome, so it is where many passengers set off by aircraft.

clue.text: Continue not working and get oneself dismissed

explanation.surface: A worker who keeps going without working, then gets the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman plays on when he hits the ball onto his own stumps and is out. 'Not working and' links, hinting at playing rather than working.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on with a game is to proceed, and a cricketer who knocks the ball into his own wicket is out.

clue.text: Composer concealing singular gift

indicators.note: concealing says the composer's name hides a letter inside it

parts.note: Handel was a German-born British composer
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A composer hides a single present.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsel is a gift given for good luck, especially at New Year or a new venture.

clue.text: Crazy conclusions from jurymen you must not query

indicators.note: conclusions from picks the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Jurors are told they must not question an insane verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is slang for mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Like a constituent, favouring one faction

explanation.surface: An MP's constituent who takes one party's side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' suggests a voter; here it means a component part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forming only a part is incomplete, and someone favouring one side is biased.

clue.text: Oriental creature has father's letters

parts.note: the letters spelling pa, a word for father; written out with the joining word they describe this clue phrase

explanation.surface: An Eastern animal holds its dad's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests mail; it means the letters making up PA, written out as P AND A.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a black-and-white bear native to China.

clue.text: Amusing show — in tragic times, can you do it?

indicators.note: tragic suggests the following words meet a disastrous fate and are scrambled

explanation.surface: A question whether a comic programme can be made in dark times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragic' rearranges TIMES CAN YOU DO IT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom is a humorous television or radio series built around recurring characters.

clue.text: Mediterranean rock plant, say

indicators.note: say tells you the plant name is pronounced and spelled differently

parts.note: scilla is a plant, the squill, of the lily family

explanation.surface: A plant found on rocks around the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: Scylla was the rock and sea monster opposite Charybdis in the Strait of Messina.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Scylla is the rock monster facing the whirlpool Charybdis across the strait between Italy and Sicily.

clue.text: Irregular and tendentious

explanation.surface: Two adjectives for an unfair account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' here means a guerrilla fighter, not an uneven thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla fighting outside a regular army is an irregular, and a one-sided, biased account is tendentious.
